findings.rationale: Update norms are about 10x the size-adjusted median in every round from round 1 (median norm_ratio 10.7, z=+11.6), and the cosine to the median update is near zero and erratic across rounds (mean_cos -0.009, ranging from -0.94 to +1). This is the signature of large random noise in uploads rather than a scaled honest update, which would keep a positive cosine. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.8275, CITL 0.016), so label noise and prevalence shift are unlikely. Poisoning was considered but a sign flip would give cos near -1 and a scaled honest update a clearly positive cos, neither of which fits.

Update norms are about 9x the size-adjusted median in every round from round 1 (median norm_ratio 9.04, z=+10.8), with cosine to the median swinging between -0.75 and +1 and averaging 0.06. This matches large random noise in uploads. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.8623, CITL 0.006), so label noise and prevalence shift are unlikely. The later HeartDisease drift flag (onset 16) is a single-feature shift that does not explain the norm anomaly from round 1.

WA, the largest client (n=11181), has update norms about 19x the median in every round from round 1 (median norm_ratio 19.24, z=+10.2), far beyond what its size predicts. Cosine to the median is weak and erratic (mean_cos 0.16, min -0.52). Local performance is normal (AUC 0.8189, CITL 0.009), pointing to noisy uploads rather than label problems.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients on updates, local performance, drift, feature tails, and subgroup outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income). Three clients (CO, MA, WA) stand out consistently: their update norms are 9 to 19 times the size-adjusted median from round 1 onward, with near-zero or erratic cosine to the median. Their local AUC and calibration are normal, which argues against label noise or prevalence shift. I classed these as explanation_instability (random-noise uploads) rather than poisoning, because the cosines do not look like sign-flipped or scaled honest updates. Confidence is moderate because the three share one signature and poisoning was not fully excluded. Other signals were not confirmed: subgroup O/E outliers (AK Sex, AR Sex, several small Income groups) were noisy and inconsistent on re-query; drift flags (MI, AK, MA) were single-feature or weak; no client showed label-noise or prevalence-shift CITL/AUC patterns; feature-tail outliers (DC, SD, NH, PR) were not consistent across tools. Budget was fully spent (20.0).
